cohort: The study included 10,616,025 live births in Brazil between January 2013 and December 2021 who weighed 500g or more at birth.
finding: The prevalence of congenital eye malformations was 12 cases per 100,000 live births, with associations found between these malformations and cesarean delivery, unsatisfactory Apgar score, birth weight < 2500g, and indigenous ethnicity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as an associated factor for the occurrence of congenital ophthalmic anomalies.
cross-section timing: Data on live births were collected between January 2013 and December 2021.
birth_weight: Live births born with >= 500g were included; birth weight < 2500g was identified as an associated factor.
